incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: high prefix/kv cache miss rate detected for inference-runtime in us-west-2. Severity: P2. Paging oncall: Marcus (oncall). Logs and metrics auto-attached.
Marcus (oncall): ack. where's the customer impact? any 5xx spike or latency SLO breaches?
Ava (eng-sre): looking. Quick summary from metrics: token latency 95p up ~2.8x for a 10m window; 5xx steady but some spike in 10:12-10:18 UTC. Pulling prefix miss time-series now.
Ava (eng-sre): link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kv/prefix-miss?panelId=3&from=2201234467&to=2201234767 (shared for triage)
Priya (svc-ops): customer-impact check: Ilya reported an alert for one enterprise tenant on us-west-2 at 10:15 — requests slowed and retries increased. Nathalie can you confirm downstream support tickets?
Nathalie (cust-success): confirming — Ticket #C-34198: multiple customers complaining about slow responses; estimated users affected ~120 orgs (sampling). Marking customers impacted: 5 flagged as high-priority. I’ll draft comms if we need an incident notification.
Marcus (oncall): ok collect logs + timeline. Ava/Luca, can you grab the rewarm/eviction events and any invalidation API calls around 10:00-10:30?
Ava (eng-sre): yes. Running query on log-warehouse:
```
select timestamp, node, event, prefix_key, reason
from kv_evictions
where timestamp between '2026-03-15T10:00:00Z' and '2026-03-15T10:30:00Z'
order by timestamp asc
limit 200;
```
Ava (eng-sre): partial results: several mass-eviction batches from autoscaler job on nodes pool-kv-12 at 10:05-10:07, then invalidation API calls triggered by rollout service at 10:08 (unknown rollout id). Attaching excerpt:
```
10:05:11 node=pool-kv-12 event=evict_batch size=128 reason=mem_pressure
10:06:02 node=pool-kv-12 event=evict_batch size=256 reason=mem_pressure
10:08:09 svc=rollout-svc call=invalidate_prefix prefixes=["user-*/session-*"] rollout_id=rop-78
```
Luca (eng-runtime): that rollout_id matches a canary config push for quantized models. The rollout service should not invalidate prefix caches globally. Investigating why that call was broad.
Marcus (oncall): hypothesis H1: aggressive eviction + broad invalidation at ~10:08 caused prefix cache misswave, KV rewarmstorm led to latency spike. H2: hot-prefix churn due to traffic pattern change amplified misses. Let's enumerate evidence we need.
Priya (svc-ops): evidence list: 1) per-prefix miss rates pre/post 10:08, 2) rewarm token QPS to origin (backing store) by node, 3) invalidation call trace and who triggered, 4) concurrent deploys/scale events. I'll own coordination with deploy team.
Ava (eng-sre): I’m pulling per-prefix miss counts: query to metrics:
```
sum(increase(kv_prefix_miss_total[5m])) by (prefix) |> sort_desc()
```
Ava (eng-sre): top offending prefixes between 10:10-10:20: `user-*/session-*` (63% of misses), `prompt-cache/v1/*` (18%), `routing/meta` (5%). That aligns to invalidation list.
Luca (eng-runtime): checking origin QPS and thundering: I see origin fetches spike ~40x after invalidation. KV nodes exhausted CPU (sys CPU) due to expensive deserialization during rewarm.
Marcus (oncall): live mitigation ideas — (a) throttle invalidation API for rollout-svc, (b) temporarily scale up kv pool or add read-replicas to absorb rewarm, (c) enable stale-while-revalidate for hot prefixes so requests don't block on origin, (d) short-circuit certain prefixes to memory-layer fallback.
Priya (svc-ops): short timeline for mitigation: immediate (T+5m) throttle invalidation, next +10m scale pool, +20m deploy S-W-R config. Which one can we do fastest?
Luca (eng-runtime): we can toggle SWR flag per-prefix via config push — low-risk, I can flip for `user-*/session-*` now. Also can spin up two spare kv instances in the pool; autoscaler can add but might be slow.
Marcus (oncall): do SWR first + throttle invalidation. Ava, can you add a temporary global rate limit to rollout-svc invalidation calls? And log the deploy id.
Ava (eng-sre): adding rate limit: `kubectl patch deployment rollout-svc -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"slo/invalidations-per-min":"5"}}}}}'` — doing now.
Ava (eng-sre): rate limit applied. rollout-svc logs show invalidation call queue drained; subsequent invalidations are rate-limited at 5/min.
Luca (eng-runtime): flipping SWR for `user-*/session-*` now:
```
PATCH /config/cache/features
{ "prefix_matches": ["user-*/session-*"], "stale_while_revalidate": 30 }
```
Luca (eng-runtime): SWR enabled. Observing immediate drop in origin synchronous fetches; latency 95p trending down.
Marcus (oncall): good. Any residual errors or customer-visible failures?
Nathalie (cust-success): customer reports show slower response times until ~10:28. After SWR and throttling, complaints reduced. I'll update the affected customer list and send an interim status update.
Ava (eng-sre): collecting logs for RCA. Notes so far:
- 10:05-10:07 mass evictions due to mem_pressure on pool-kv-12
- 10:08 broad invalidation by rollout-svc (rop-78)
- 10:09-10:18 high origin fetch QPS (re-warm) causing CPU exhaustion on kv nodes
- 10:12 latency 95p peaks and a short 5xx spike
- 10:20 mitigations applied (SWR + invalidation throttle) saw recovery by 10:28
Marcus (oncall): documented timeline. Next: hypothesis validation steps.
Luca (eng-runtime): validate H1: correlate invalidation call with rewarm spike per-prefix. I’ll join logs between rollout-svc trace id and kv origin fetch traces.
Ava (eng-sre): validate H2: confirm traffic shift — looking at ingress logs: sudden burst of session creation events from a client IP block at 10:04-10:06, possibly test traffic from partner. Adding to timeline.
Priya (svc-ops): contacting deploy team: @deploy-team who triggered `rop-78`? Please respond in-thread. We need the intent — was it targeted or global?
deploy-team-bot: rop-78 corresponds to config push to quantized-models canary; change scope was intended for `model-family: quantized-v2` only. Investigation: cause of broad invalidation trace is likely a fallback path in rollout-svc that computed prefixes too broadly when scope tag absent.
Marcus (oncall): assign owners for RCA writeup: Ava — infra timeline + logs, Luca — runtime traces + mitigation playbook, Priya — deploy flow & scope bug, Nathalie — customer impact and comms. I'll draft the incident header.
Nathalie (cust-success): prepping interim customer note: ETA for full RCA EOD. Will include mitigation steps and affected customer list.
Ava (eng-sre): collecting all log excerpts and will upload a sanitized bundle: s3://redwood-incident-logs/2201234567/evictions.log and kv_origin_fetches.csv
Luca (eng-runtime): adding follow-up runbook suggestion: validate invalidation scope calculation in rollout-svc, add unit tests for prefix pattern generation, and add per-service rate-limits by default.
Marcus (oncall): final quick check — CPU usage on pool-kv normalized? Ava?
Ava (eng-sre): yes CPU back to baseline ~10:30; 95p latency ~1.1x baseline. We'll keep monitoring for next 2 hours.
Marcus (oncall): handoff at 11:00 UTC to next oncall (Luca) for postmortem collection. Marking this thread as active RCA. Thanks everyone.
Priya (svc-ops): filing follow-up action items in ops board: OP-7688 (safety-net rate-limits), OP-7689 (SWR per-prefix flagging UI), OP-7690 (deploy-svc scope bug fix). Assigning owners as agreed.
Nathalie (cust-success): sent interim status to affected customers. Will post final RPM when RCA complete.
incident-bot: Incident status changed -> Mitigated. Channel: #incidents. Link to incident doc: https://docs.redwood/internal/incidents/2201234567
Marcus (oncall): closing thread soon. If anything else pops up, re-open or ping. :thumbsup:
